text.p: Turkish central bank funded banks at the close on Wednesday after draining cash via open market operation in the morning.

The central bank lent 25 trillion lira overnight at 80 percent at close on the interbank, down from the 49.2 trillion it funded on Tuesday. Overnight money earlier traded between 77.5 and 79.75 percent.

The bank drained 29.3 trillion lira through a five-day reverse repo auction at 79.10 percent average rate on the open market in the morning. It had injected 16.5 trillion lira through a six-day repo auction at 77.45 percent on Tuesday.
The central bank had raised its overnight bid and offer rates to 55-80 percent from 50-75 percent at the opening to curb the lira's fall against the dollar.

The lira closed easier at 99,350 against the dollar versus Tuesday's 99,325 on higher central bank dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign exchange transfers, despite banks' dollar sales and lower dollar/mark parity.
The central bank gradually raised its dollar rate for banks' forex transfers to 99,250 lira from Monday's 99,050 close.
The lira firmed to 99,325 in the morning from an opening of 99,570 after the central bank raised its overnight rates.

Bankers said dollar demand was firm in the last two weeks amid expectations of higher inflation, banks' moves to take positions as the year-end nears and the central bank's relatively lower overnight lending rate.
The central bank frequently intervened in the last two weeks to suppress the U.S. currency's rise.

Yields on t-bills and bonds with longer maturities rose by as much as two points on Wednesday after the jump in Tuesday's 182-day bill auction yield while those on shorter maturity bills eased slightly.

The Treasury sold 51.49 trillion lira worth May 21, 1997 bills yesterday, with the maximum yield jumping to 144.92 percent (including witholding tax) from 135.16 in the previous 182-day bill auction on November 12.
The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper rose to 125.38 from Tuesday's 123.95.
The second most active May 21, 1997 paper yielded 126.38 percent (excluding witholding tax), little changed from 126.36 percent auction yield.
Yields in the last three Treasury bill auctions included a 10 percent witholding tax, following a cabinet decree imposing the tax on interest income from state papers issued after November 1.
But their yields on the bond market exclude the tax charge to allow comparison with papers not subject to the tax.
